references.text: The sin offering with a goat on the Day of Atonement is described here, which is the same 'chatt'at hakkippurim' (atonement sin offering) mentioned in the verse.
A detailed description of how the goat as a sin offering was to be sacrificed on the Day of Atonement to make atonement for the sanctuary.
Parallel to the sin offering with one goat that was to be offered in addition to the daily burnt offering.
The preceding verses in the same chapter describing the burnt offering on the Day of Atonement, to which this sin offering is added.
Description of the daily burnt offering (olat hatamid) with its accompanying grain offering and drink offering, mentioned as 'in addition to' in the verse.
Basic instructions for the daily burnt offering (olat hatamid) that was to be offered every morning and evening.
The laws concerning the sin offering with a goat for unintentional sins.
Hebrews refers to the Day of Atonement sacrifice where the high priest entered the Most Holy Place with blood for his own sins and those of the people.
Christ is compared to the Day of Atonement sacrifice, but with His own blood instead of the blood of goats and calves.
